evidence.M7: round0 §5.2: CO-S01 and CO-S16 are graded on their words only by 'Refund id reported' (code, refund id only). 'Refund status reported' is used by CO-S19 alone, so an agent that says 'issued' for the pending RF-5531 in CO-S16 rows 2-3 (known failure case 3: 'Final message must match the final refund status') or in CO-S01 passes, against G-03 and the must-not 'tell the customer a refund is pending or issued when the order system has not shown it'. CO-S19 asserting the clause does not cover these success exits.
evidence.N1: round1 G-03 (line 24): 'Otherwise it tells the customer the action was not done or, when it cannot tell, that the outcome is unknown'. This requires 'no refund was issued' in CO-S14/CO-S15, where no CO-A3 was made. §2 'wants to be told truthfully whether the order was cancelled' supports 'the order is cancelled' in CO-S19, where CO-A2 returned cancelled. Both rubric clauses therefore have spec support and are not unsupported claims.
evidence.P4: round2 §5.1 line 1588: values are compared 'on equality', and 'A question about only some of those values is not the confirmation question'. Appendix A line 1648: 'A payment method compares by card brand and last four digits'. A question without the brand, or one that says only 'original payment method', is either partial or unequal, so the simulated user deflects it under either reading and no verdict splits.
